b: I basically want something that is simply DUMB / inexpensive to have a spare of / but generally reliable that doesn't have its own patch cycle.

I am looking at this for two different reasons, one is to create a separate management path and the other is for cases where I want to uplink an HA pair behind this ISP device but don't want it to be dependant on a managed switch stack down stream.
This is for a branch office configuration so good and reasonably priced is the goal.
Looks like netgear is a top pick with all check out the HP model suggested as well as some others.

And while I welcome additional replies I don't really want to keep getting into the WHY, I just want a durable device that passes layer 2 traffic well. I am just trying to split a single connection to accommodate 2-3 devices downstream and yes I have the IPs to do this is connection allocates me multiple STATIC IPs. (clearing MAC addresses isn't an issue)

For reference I have built several variations over the years, with dumb switches, vLans on the main core, and a managed switch on the outside. The key problem once you go with a managed switch is that you introduce the potential of vLAN hopping vulnerabilities, and at the very least another managed device to patch even if using it in a dumb capacity.

The Dumb switch is perfectly acceptable to meet all requirements as long as it is a reliable device, which is why I asked here in the first place. AS some pointed out some dumb switches are janky, but that doesn't mean all dumb switches are.
